_note: Two meshes: the fuselage, and one lump holding the wing, both nacelles and both proprotors. So the wing has to be a cut. Because the nacelles live on the wingtips, taking the wing off takes the proprotors with it - which is exactly what would happen to the real aircraft.

wing.comment: Measured with scripts/measure-band.py. Keeping the nacelles and proprotors is deliberate - they are bolted to the wingtips and would go with the wing on the real aircraft - but the open slab was also taking the sponsons and the gear, 2595 of the 5636 vertices outboard of the fuselage.
